extracted.intended_audience: principal investigators and researchers preparing grant proposal resubmissions (University of Utah researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for revising and resubmitting a declined grant proposal, including general best practices and sponsor-specific notes for NSF and NIH. Advises how to use reviewer comments, interact with program officers, and decide between resubmission, new submission, or alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request reviewer comments promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Request reviewer comments as soon as they are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain the reviewers' critiques so you understand the reasons for decline and can target revisions. The page emphasizes requesting comments immediately after they are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult Program Officer for clarification and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow up with the Program Officer (PO) for additional clarification, guidance, or suggestions about resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Officers can offer clarification on reviewer feedback and advice about whether and how to resubmit; contacting them is recommended as an early step in deciding next actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: If sponsor discourages resubmission, pursue alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sponsor discourages resubmission, identify alternative funding sources or revise the project scope or approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If told not to resubmit, you may need to find other sponsors or change the project's aims/approach. The Program Officer, colleagues, and OSP can help assess these options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address each reviewer comment explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing a revised application, address each reviewer's comment explicitly in your narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to every critique point-by-point in the application text (or response-to-reviewers section) so reviewers and staff can see how you handled concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight changes made to strengthen the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight what you have changed to strengthen the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it easy for reviewers to find revisions by clearly indicating where and how the application was changed compared to the prior submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify misunderstandings from the initial review
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify any areas that may have been misunderstood in the initial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewers misread or misunderstood aspects of the project, explicitly restate or reframe those elements to prevent repeat misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be open to constructive feedback and refine aims/methods/framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Stay open to constructive feedback and be willing to refine the project's aims, methods, or framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective reassessment and willingness to change substantive elements (aims, methods, framing) can materially improve competitiveness on resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate closely with the Program Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Close collaboration with your Program Officer and a willingness to objectively reassess your proposal greatly enhance resubmission competitiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with the PO throughout revision planning—their input can guide which changes will be meaningful to the program and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF: treat resubmissions as new submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF does not have a formal resubmission mechanism; each proposal — revised or not — is treated as a new submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Directors are not required to compare your application to a previously declined version and may not realize it is a revision unless you proactively frame it that way in your narrative. If you want prior reviewers to see changes, explicitly describe them in the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF: request reconsideration if review handled inappropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: If you believe the review was not handled appropriately, NSF policy allows you to request reconsideration by the cognizant Assistant Director or Office Head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This process evaluates whether the review was fair procedurally and substantively. Refer to the NSF Proposal & Award Policies & Procedures Guide (PAPPG) for full details on the reconsideration process and which decisions are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH: use the formal resubmission (A1) mechanism and consider options
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH uses a formal resubmission process; revised applications are designated with an 'A1' indicator. NIH provides guidance on whether to revise and resubmit, appeal, submit a new (A0) proposal instead, or seek alternative funding mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before resubmitting to NIH, use NIH's structured tools, guidance pages, and flow charts to determine the proper path for your situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH: review Summary Statement and consult PO; use NIH/CSR resources
rubrics_metrics.description: If your NIH application is not funded, review the Summary Statement and any posted scores or critiques and consult your Program Officer for guidance on whether a resubmission is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NIH’s structured tools and the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) resources to understand how applications are evaluated and to interpret review outcomes when deciding next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission generally can succeed after revision
rubrics_metrics.description: If your proposal was not funded, a thoughtful, well targeted resubmission often has a strong chance of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page encourages applicants not to be discouraged and notes that many successful awards result from revising an earlier submission and applying again—either to the same sponsor or a different one.
